text.p: Swiss shares broke from their recent record run to end below the 5,000 point-level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after Nestle's first quarter results triggered profit taking on a broad front.
"The correction is only normal after the recent strong rise," one dealer said.

He said the downward trend may continue for a while before prices hit levels low enough to bring investors back into the market. Further developments would also depend on Wall Street, one trader added.
The SMI slipped 41.2 points, or 0.82 percent, to end at 4,988.4 and the broad Swiss Performance Index dropped 19.74 points, or 0.62 percent, to 3,150.82.
Bourse volume totally a relatively high 2.82 billion francs.
Dealers said an early rise of the market was thwarted by Nestle's dissappointing first quarter sales figures and the subsequent drop in the stock.
The market had expected a currency related rise of at least 20 percent, but sales rose a reported 18.7 percent. Nestle shares slumped 40 francs, or 2.17 percent, to close at 1,802.
Novartis registered shares, which led the actives list, lost 19 francs to end at 1,991.
Roche certificates jumped 45 francs to 12,735 after repeating their profit expectations for 1997.
ABB, Holderbank and SMH also saw gains.
Among major banks, CS Group lost 2.5 percent, or 4.25 francs, to finish at 168. UBS bearers ended lower after the recent rise, slipping 18 francs to 1,390.

Volume was high in the stocks of chemical company Ems, which ended unchanged at 6,125 francs. Ems-Chemie Holding AG, which bought shares in March rather than paying a dividend, said it was now offering to buy a further 14,140 bearer shares at 6,100 Swiss francs per share.
